string.text: Kill the boss yourself and the coordinates of a rare (yellow) stash on the current map come through on your PDA, filled by the game's own stash system. If the map has no free stash left, they come on the next map that has one. Default on.

Sets every slider that makes the game easier or harder at once: hunt timing, squad size and named hunters, how many maps they follow, retreat health, accuracy, damage reduction, escalation, the boss and the emission boss. Check boxes, volumes and effects are not touched. Medium is the defaults; Easy is about 20% easier, Hard about 20% harder. Change any of those by hand and this shows Custom. Picking a difficulty again overwrites them. Default Medium.
Loudness of the teleport sound when a hunter breaks off or vanishes. 0 mutes it. Default 40.

A psy hum coming from the nearest named hunter, a sound you can place by ear: this volume within 10 m of him, fading out by 100 m. A named hunter is the main Nemesis enemy: hard to kill, he retreats when hurt and comes back stronger. 0 mutes it. Default 10.
Loudness of the radio static that comes with the arrival warning. 0 mutes it. Default 70.
Radio static (for the boss also psy voices) 30 to 120 seconds before a hunt starts. With this or the PDA warning on, the hunt follows the warning; with both off it starts without one. Default on.
A PDA message from an unknown frequency 30 to 120 seconds before a hunt starts. With this or the audio warning on, the hunt follows the warning; with both off it starts without one. Default off.

Loudness of the lightning strike sound when the emission boss arrives. The emission is already loud, so it is off by default; his teleport burst (Teleport volume) marks his arrival. 0 mutes it. Default 0.
Name of the Monolith boss, a rare and stronger named hunter who fights to the death. Other hunters always get random names. Default: Bogdan Kravets
Name of the UNISG boss, their best fighter, who hunts Monolith, Zombified and Sin players. Default: Lyutomyr Kat

Chance that a hunt brings the boss: a tougher, cloaked hunter with his own look and messages and an escort. It climbs by 2 every 4 hunts without him, and the 30th hunt without him brings him for sure. Only one boss at a time, at most one a day. Beating a hunt he was in halves the escalation. 0 = no boss at all. Default 4.

How much less damage the boss (Monolith or UNISG) takes from every hit, on top of his armour and the escalation. He never retreats: he fights until he or you are dead. 0 = like any stalker in his armour. Default 30.
How many of the boss's first shots at you in a hunt always miss, a moment to react. Both bosses. 0 turns it off. Default 2.

How hard the boss hits other stalkers and mutants, in percent of a normal hit. He fights anyone who fights him, but always prefers you; this makes him a killer against them. Your own damage from him is not affected. Default 200.

How many named hunters come with the boss. They hunt you like any named hunter, the real threat and distraction, while he sneaks up to finish you. A boss hunt ignores Squad of 1 to 5 and Extra is a named hunter. 0 = he comes alone. Default 4.

A gentle wave over your screen while the boss is near: it starts softly at 60 m and grows to this strength at 5 m. It works while he is cloaked too, and fades out when he dies. 0 turns it off. Default 40.
In-game days after the grace period before a boss can appear. Default 7.
Use the high definition portrait on PDA messages. Off uses the original low definition icon.

For testing: hunts start sooner (no grace period, 120 seconds between hunts, 15 seconds from the warning to the hunt) and can spawn anywhere, even near traders and bases. A red map marker follows the boss. Turn it off for normal play.

Tick and apply before you remove the mod: any running hunt is called off, every Nemesis squad is removed from the world, and no new hunt starts while the box stays ticked. A PDA message tells you when it is safe to save. Then save, remove the mod and load that save. Untick it to let the hunts come back.

Only with the Wearable Devices mod installed: when a hunt spawns, your device screens flicker at random for about 2.5 seconds. When the boss spawns, they also go black for 2 seconds after it. Without that mod this does nothing. Default on.
Write Nemesis diagnostic and error lines to the console. Leave this off unless you are tracking a problem. Lines that start with an exclamation mark are errors.
In-game days before the first hunt of a new game (or after installing the mod). Default 18.
In-game hours after a hunt ends before the next one can start. 0 = as soon as possible. Default 36.
If you survive this many in-game hours, the hunters give up and teleport away, and the next hunt is not stronger. Default 5.
A named hunter breaks off and teleports away when his health drops this low. It is the same in every cycle. The bosses never retreat. Default 30.

Each hunt you beat makes the next one stronger. That step is called a cycle. Each cycle after the first adds this much damage reduction to named hunters and bosses, up to Max escalation. 0 = no growth. Default 2.
The most damage reduction the cycles can ever add, however many hunts you beat. At the defaults it is reached at cycle 11. Default 20.

How many more of their shots hit you at range than a normal stalker with the same weapon, in percent. Named hunters get this value, regular squad members half of it, and the boss this value plus 15. 0 turns it off. Default 10.

How much less damage the regular squad members take, from every hit, the killing one too: yours, other NPCs' and mutants'. They keep their own armour. It does not grow with the cycle. 0 makes them normal stalkers, who die to a headshot. Default 0.
How much less damage named hunters take from every hit, on top of their armour (a copy of yours) and the escalation. Default 25.
Halve escalation when a hunter kills you
If a hunter kills you, the escalation is halved (cycle 8 becomes 4, never below 1), even when you reload a save. Default on.
This will load your last saved custom settings. They are saved automatically when a difficulty setting is applied. The backup is kept, and the box unticks itself.
Tick and apply to set the hunts back to their starting strength (cycle 1) right now. The box unticks itself.

The most of a hit's damage (yours or an NPC's) a hunt member can ever shrug off, however BR mitigation, damage reduction and escalation stack. At 70 they always take at least 30% of it, so a long run never becomes unwinnable. The armour class itself works through GAMMA ballistics on your bullets and comes on top. Default 70.

Named hunters and bosses wear a copy of your armour class (BR). This much is added to it, and to the regular squad members' own armour, from their second hit on a body part (GAMMA ballistics loads it on the first). The same in every cycle. Needs GAMMA ballistics. Default 0.
Named hunters and bosses copy your armour's mitigation (BR%). This much is added to it, and to the regular squad members'. They never block more than 90 percent. The same in every cycle. Default 0.

Nemesis stalkers you kill are not looted by NPCs. With AlifePlus installed, its own "reserve own kills" option decides (its range and time apply), and nothing is reserved while that option is off. Without AlifePlus a body stays yours for 2 in-game hours, or until you have been more than 150 m away from it for 3 minutes. On by default.

For testing. Pick one and apply: Boss brings the boss in the next hunt, ignoring the chance, the day limit and the once-a-day rule. Emission boss brings him now, even without an emission (a running hunt is called off for him; get indoors to see the haunted exits). It acts once and goes back to None. Default None.

On the newest demonized exes, hunters use new engine features where they help: named hunters and the boss prefer you as their target and turn on whoever shoots them, and a retreating hunter is held in place by the engine for his teleport. On older exes, or with this off, the mod's own way is used. Default on.

How strongly a named hunter turns on whoever just shot him, within 60 m. On the engine's own scale, the pull toward the player when the player sees him is 900, and you count double for hunters. Higher: they turn on NPC attackers more readily. 0 leaves it to the engine. Needs Latest exe AI features and the newest demonized exes. Default 600.
The same for the boss. Kept low so he fights back but stays on you; for 5 seconds after you hurt him he ignores other NPCs anyway. 0 leaves it to the engine. Default 300.

On: when a hunter loses track of you, he searches where he last saw or heard you, and finds you again after 60 seconds. Off: hunters always head for where you are until they see you; then they fight. Default on.

Extra squad members approach from the sides on clear lanes instead of running straight at you, and those carrying sniper rifles stop short and take a firing position. Named hunters still come straight for you. Default on.
How many times a hunt follows you to another map. After that, the next change of map shakes them off. 0: they never follow, and a change of map ends the hunt as an escape. Default 2.
Before teleporting away, a hurt hunter first flees away from you to cover (or, without cover, along a clear lane) for up to 4 seconds. He cannot be hurt while he runs. Default on.

Named hunters turn invisible while they stalk you from more than 30 m, and reappear when they fight, get within 15 m or take a hit that does damage. At most once every 20 seconds. While cloaked, other stalkers ignore them. Uses the same invisible model as the teleport. Experimental: a held weapon may stay visible. Default on.
Hunters stop chasing and start fighting when they see you, or any other enemy, this close. Default 100.
Hunters (the emission boss too) never spawn closer to you than this. Default 80.
The farthest from you a hunt (the emission boss too) can spawn. Default 140.
Relative chance the hunt is only the hunter. These five sliders are weights, not percents, so they do not need to add up to 100. Default 50.
Relative chance he brings one extra normal stalker. The extra can be killed. Default 25.
Relative chance of two extras with him. Default 14.
Relative chance of three extras with him. Default 10.
Relative chance of four extras with him. Default 6. Set a weight to 0 to stop that squad size.

Chance that each extra squad member is another named hunter instead of a normal stalker. Named hunters carry a rank in their name, are hard to kill and retreat when hurt. 0 = only the leader is named, 100 = the whole squad. Default 15.

On: hunts in rookie areas are smaller (Cordon and Swamps: at most 2 hunters; Garbage, Dark Valley and similar: at most 3), and in late areas extras are more often named hunters (+10 in Red Forest, Radar and similar; +20 in Pripyat, Jupiter, Zaton and the CNPP). Boss hunts are not affected. Default on.
